objective: Prove that every stage of band growth (the n x 2 ladder and every n x m torus) reads the cut length D and the time length g*delta + 1 exactly; that the plain first need is on time on the n x m torus (n <= m) exactly when n <= 2 or n = m = 3 (the ladder by its unique shortest routes, thick tori by the systole lemma of PLAIN-TIME-20261108-001B on the plane and on the cylinders of width 3 to 5, small tori read exactly); give the balls of both lengths on the cylinder and the torus in closed form; and compute the plain first need on every torus of the square, triangular and honeycomb lattices, not only the rotation-invariant ones, to the index stated.
status: Proved 2026-11-09 (by hand; finite claims checked exactly; the census of every torus computed): every stage of band growth reads the cut length D and the time length g*delta + 1 exactly; every square torus holding (0,2) or (2,0), the n x 2 ladder and its twisted forms, is on time without freezing at every size; the n x m torus (2 <= n <= m) is on time exactly when n = 2 or n = m = 3, so every stage from the second band on is late but 3 x 3; ring and time balls in closed form, 2r^2 + 2r + 1 out to half the loop, then 2n per step (a tube). Computed to index 100, 80 and 50: the square (2,1) tubes of one chirality and the triangular sqrt 3 tubes are on time too, and every other on-time torus is small; PLAIN-TIME-20261108-001B's 26 tori are the rotation-invariant ones (correction).
title: The grown torus reads distance by freezing at every stage, and plainly only as a ladder
